metadata.summary: Kevin Pietersen is “buzzing” to be back with the England set-up, having joined the white-ball coaching staff for the series against Sri Lanka, according to interim head coach Marcus Trescothick.
metadata.content: Kevin Pietersen 'buzzing' at England white-ball coaching role as specialist mentor, says Marcus Trescothick | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Kevin Pietersen 'buzzing' at England white-ball coaching role as specialist mentor, says Marcus Trescothick Kevin Pietersen "buzzing" for England role and will add "a little more spark" to white-ball sides, says batting coach Marcus Trescothick; watch the first T20I against Sri Lanka in Southampton, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, Tuesday (first ball 6.30pm) Monday 14 September 2026 06:08, UK Image: Kevin Pietersen has been appointed as a ‘specialist mentor’ to England’s white-ball teams Kevin Pietersen is “buzzing” to be back with the England set-up, having joined the white-ball coaching staff for the series against Sri Lanka, according to interim head coach Marcus Trescothick. Pietersen will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa next year. He will link up with the squad this week ahead of England's first T20I against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, with the first ball at 6.30pm. Trescothick and Pietersen were Ashes-winning team-mates during England's famous 2005 triumph, giving the former first-hand experience of the qualities and talents the latter can bring to the current team. The German proved too strong for the eighth-seeded American prevailing 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 in the final at Flushing Meadows. Zverev added the New York title to his collection after winning the French Open earlier this year. In a bizarre ending, Shelton's return sailed long on match point, but Zverev, seemingly unaware that he had won, hit the balls back to the other end of the court, ready for another game. It was only when Zverev glanced up at the big screen that he realised he had actually won. messages.text: Wade ends 10-year European title drought with victory in Flanders

metadata.summary: James Wade ended a decade-long wait for a European Tour title as he beat Ross Smith 8-4 in the final of the Flanders Darts Trophy.
metadata.content: Flanders Darts Trophy: James Wade ends 10-year wait for European Tour title with win over Ross Smith in Antwerp | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content Flanders Darts Trophy: James Wade ends 10-year wait for European Tour title with win over Ross Smith in Antwerp Wade played in the first European Tour final in 2012 and was victorious in the 150th event this weekend; Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Grand Prix coming up from September 28-October 4 Sunday 13 September 2026 22:50, UK Image: James Wade won the Flanders Darts Trophy on Sunday (Pic: James O'Connor/PDC) James Wade ended a decade-long wait for a European Tour title as he beat Ross Smith 8-4 in the final of the Flanders Darts Trophy. The 43-year-old, who last tasted continental glory at the European Darts Matchplay in Hamburg in 2016, produced a 95.50 average and five 180s in the final in Antwerp on Sunday evening. Earlier in the day he'd beaten Damon Heta 7-4 in the semi-final, having whitewashed Danny Noppert 6-0 in the quarter-finals and edging Rob Cross 6-5 in the last 16. metadata.summary: Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.
metadata.content: Erling Haaland’s Man City goal decision vs Man Utd an ‘error of judgement', says Pro Ref | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Erling Haaland’s Man City goal decision vs Man Utd an ‘error of judgement', says Pro Ref Refereeing body Pro Ref admits "error of judgment" in awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd; Pro Ref has contacted Man Utd and revealed Erling Haaland's goal "should have recommended an on-field review"; Haaland's second-half winner secured a 1-0 win for 10-man Man City at Old Trafford Sunday 13 September 2026 23:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Erling Haaland's controversial winner for Man City at Man Utd Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford. In a statement released just hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref revealed it had made contact with Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner. The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision. The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.
